question.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{E}[3X-4].$

$$
f(x)=\frac{x}{8}-\frac{1}{4},\,2<x<6
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we simplify using the properties of expected value:

$$
\text{E}[3X-4]=3\text{E}[X]-4
$$

For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the expected value using the following formula:

$$
\text{E}[X]={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we calculate the expected value of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{6}x\cdot (\frac{x}{8}-\frac{1}{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{6}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}-\frac{x}{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{{x}^{3}}{24}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{8})|}_{2}^{6} \\  & =\frac{9}{2}-(-\frac{1}{6}) \\  & =\frac{14}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[3X-4] & =3\text{E}[X]-4 \\  & =3\cdot \frac{14}{3}-4 \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$
